questions.q: Punctuation Galore. Write a text explaining the concept of deadlocks in computer science using as many different punctuation marks as possible. Use them correctly. Your text should be at most 250 words long.
questions.qzh: 用尽可能多种标点 (正确地!) 写一段不超过 250 词的文字, 解释计算机科学 里的死锁.
questions.a:
What happens when two processes wait for each other—forever? Consider processes P and Q, each of which needs two resources (say, a printer and a file). P locks the printer; Q locks the file. Now P requests the file, while Q requests the printer: neither can proceed. This situation is called a deadlock.

Coffman et al. (1971) identified four necessary conditions: (1) mutual exclusion; (2) hold and wait; (3) no preemption; and (4) circular wait. If any one of them is broken, deadlock is impossible. For example, if every process acquires resources in a fixed global order (“printer before file”), a cycle cannot form.

Operating systems use three strategies: prevention, avoidance (e.g., the banker’s algorithm), and detection-and-recovery. Detection builds a wait-for graph and searches it for cycles; recovery then aborts a process or preempts a resource … with all the trouble that entails!

用到的标点: 问号、em dash、句号、逗号、括号、分号、冒号、斜体术语、复数所有格 (banker’s)、et al. 的缩写点、编号括号、引号、e.g. 的缩写点和逗号、连字符 (detection-and-recovery、wait-for)、省略号、感叹号. 写完后对照第 6、7 讲逐个检查用法是否正确, 比堆数量更重要.

questions.q: Types of Commas. Identify the type of each comma (e.g., introductory, gapping) in the following text: Okay, Dave, let’s be clear: Patrick, Rachel, and Sophia have all voiced concerns, and Liz filed a formal complaint. At the last meeting, you ate chocolate-dipped pickles in front of everyone. You didn’t offer to share, though, and that’s unacceptable. RamsesThePigeon, “Wordsmithing 101: Comma Chameleon,” YouTube, 2024, https://youtu.be/zJQKrrhdnsU .
questions.qzh: 按第 7 讲的八种逗号 (列举、连接、系列、括入、引导、分隔、省略、呼语) 判断每个逗号的类型. 例句: 「好吧, Dave, 咱们把话说清楚: Patrick、Rachel 和 Sophia 都表示过不满, Liz 还正式投诉了. 上次开会, 你当着所有人的面吃蘸了巧克力的腌黄瓜. 不过你没请大家一起吃, 这可不行.」
questions.a:
1. 「Okay,」: 引导逗号 (句首的感叹词 Okay).
  2. 「Dave,」: 呼语逗号 (称呼对方的名字; 和前一个逗号一起把 Dave 括起来, 前一个逗号也兼作呼语逗号).
  3. 「Patrick,」: 列举逗号.
  4. 「Rachel, and Sophia」: 系列逗号 (Oxford comma).
  5. 「concerns, and Liz filed」: 连接逗号 (and 连接两个独立分句).
  6. 「At the last meeting,」: 引导逗号 (句首的状语短语).
  7. 「share, though,」: 这一对把插入的 though 括起来, 是括入逗号; 第二个逗号同时也是 and 前面连接两个独立分句的连接逗号 (You didn’t offer to share … and that’s unacceptable), 一个逗号兼两职.

这段话里没有分隔逗号和省略逗号.

questions.q: Missing Hyphens. The following paragraph lacks hyphens. Add them where necessary following either American or British conventions, whichever you prefer. The Institute for Informatics is looking for applicants for a full professorship in one of the following areas: algorithm design, data structures, artificial intelligence, and cyber security. The position requires problem solving skills, logical thinking, and hands on experience with high level programming languages such as Pascal and Modula 2. The successful applicant will be expected to teach courses on scalable networks, high performance software, and low level system development. She or he should share the institute’s vision of computer science as the cornerstone of our technology driven society.
questions.qzh: 一则招聘教授的启事里所有连字符都被删掉了, 按美式或英式规范补上.
questions.a:
需要连字符的 (复合形容词放在名词前作定语): problem-solving skills、hands-on experience、high-level programming languages、high-performance software、low-level system development、technology-driven society; 语言名 Modula-2 本身带连字符.

不需要的: full professorship、algorithm design、data structures、artificial intelligence、scalable networks (都是固定名词词组或「形容词 + 名词」, 不是放在另一个名词前的复合修饰语). cyber security: 美式通常写成一个词 cybersecurity, 英式多写作两个词 cyber security, 都不用连字符 (cyber-security 也能见到, 但不常用).

questions.q: Commas Galore. Write a text arguing the merits of either static type systems (as found in, e.g., C++ and Java) or dynamic type systems (as found in, e.g., JavaScript and Python) using as many different types of commas as possible. Use them correctly. Your text should be at most 250 words long.
questions.qzh: 写一段不超过 250 词的文字, 论证静态类型系统 (C++、Java) 或动态类型系统 (JavaScript、Python) 的优点, 尽量用上各种类型的逗号, 而且用对.
questions.a:
Frankly, dear reader, static typing is worth its cost. A type checker catches misspelled fields, missing cases, and mismatched arguments before the program ever runs, and it does so for every execution, not just the tested ones. Types also document code: a signature such as List<Order> findOrders(Customer c) tells the reader what goes in and what comes out. In large projects, this documentation never goes stale, because the compiler checks it. Refactoring, which is risky in dynamic languages, becomes routine; renaming a method, the IDE updates every caller, and the compiler confirms the result. Java has nominal types, TypeScript structural ones.

用到的逗号: Frankly, (引导) dear reader, (呼语); fields, cases, (列举) cases, and (系列); runs, and it (连接); execution, not just (分隔/对比); In large projects, (引导); stale, because (分隔从句); Refactoring, which … languages, (括入); Java has nominal types, TypeScript structural ones (省略 gapping: 省掉了 has). (「renaming a method, the IDE …」这类悬垂分词不要写, 这里只为演示; 正确写法是 when you rename a method, the IDE …)

questions.q: Telephone Game. The following two pages present the Java code for the bubble sort and selection sort algorithms. Form a pair with another student. Assign one of the algorithms to you and the other one to your teammate. Read your algorithm and only that one. Write a description of the inner workings of your algorithm. You can assume that the reader knows about the swap function. Exchange the descriptions once you and your teammate have finished writing. Write a Java program that exactly follows your teammate’s description. Once you and your teammate have finished programming, exchange your programs and compare them with those given on the following pages. Discuss how effective the descriptions were at conveying the algorithms. static public void bubbleSort ( int [] a) { final int n = a. length ; for ( int i = 0 ; i < n; i++) { for ( int j = 0 ; j < n - i - 1 ; j++) { if (a[j] > a[j + 1 ]) { swap(a, j, j + 1 ); } } } } static public void selectionSort ( int [] a) { final int n = a. length ; for ( int i = 0 ; i < n - 1 ; i++) { int min = i; for ( int j = i + 1 ; j < n; j++) { if (a[j] < a[min]) { min = j; } } if (min > i) { swap(a, i, min); } } }
questions.qzh: 两人一组的「传话」: 每人只读一种排序算法 (冒泡排序或选择排序) 的代码, 用文字描述它的工作方式; 交换描述后, 严格按对方的文字写出 Java 程序, 再和原代码对比, 讨论描述传达得好不好.
questions.a:
两段参考描述:

Bubble sort. The algorithm makes n passes over the array a of length n. In pass i (counting from 0), it compares each pair of neighbors a[j] and a[j + 1] for j from 0 to n − i − 2 and swaps them if a[j] > a[j + 1]. After pass i, the i + 1 largest elements are in their final positions at the end of the array, so each pass can stop one position earlier than the previous one.

Selection sort. For each position i from 0 to n − 2, the algorithm finds the index min of the smallest element among a[i], …, a[n − 1]; if several elements are equally small, it takes the first one. If min differs from i, it swaps a[i] and a[min]. Afterwards, a[0], …, a[i] contain the i + 1 smallest elements in ascending order.

讨论时最常暴露的问题: 下标从 0 还是 1 开始、区间是否包含端点 (n − i − 1 是上界还是最后一个下标)、比较用 > 还是 ≥ (决定了排序是否稳定、相等元素是否交换)、外层循环跑 n 次还是 n − 1 次. 好的描述要说清这些边界, 并给出循环不变式 (每趟之后什么成立), 读者才能复现完全相同的程序.

questions.q: Cite and Quote. Write a paragraph of at most 200 words explaining generics in the Java programming language. Include at least one citation, one naming of authors, one reference, and one quotation. Potential reference material includes the following: The Java® Language Specification ( https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se21/html/index.html ) The Java™ Tutorials: Generics ( https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/extra/generics/index.html ) Java® Platform, Standard Edition & Java Development Kit ( https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/index.html )
questions.qzh: 写一段不超过 200 词的文字介绍 Java 泛型, 至少包含一处引用 (citation)、一处点出作者姓名、一条参考文献条目、一处直接引语 (quotation).
questions.a:
结构示例 (引语内容请自己从来源里逐字摘录, 下面用 [quotation] 占位, 不要凭记忆写引语):

Generics allow classes, interfaces, and methods to be parameterized by types. For example, List<String> denotes a list whose elements are strings, so the compiler can reject an attempt to insert an Integer and no cast is needed when an element is retrieved. The Java Language Specification [1, Section 8.1.2] defines a generic class as one that declares type variables, and Bracha’s generics tutorial [2] explains the motivation: “[quotation].” Generics are implemented by erasure: type arguments are checked at compile time and then removed, which is why new T() is not allowed.

[1] James Gosling et al. The Java Language Specification, Java SE 21 Edition. Oracle, 2023. URL: …
[2] Gilad Bracha. “Generics in the Java Programming Language.” In: The Java Tutorials. Oracle. URL: …

对照题目要求逐项检查: 引用 = 正文里的 [1]; 点出作者 = Bracha’s; 参考文献 = 文末条目; 引语 = 逐字摘录并加引号、标出处. 作者和年份以你实际打开的页面为准 (教程页底有作者信息).

questions.q: Explaining a Topic. For each of the following two papers, write a text of about 250 words that explains the topic using appropriate citations and quotations to acknowledge the paper as your source. You will probably not need to do a close reading of the papers. Han Qiao et al. “To use or not to use: Impatience and overreliance when using generative AI productivity support tools.” In: CHI 2025. ACM, 2025. URL: https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3706598.3714103 Jeffrey Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat. “MapReduce: Simplified data processing on large clusters.” In: OSDI 2004. USENIX Association, 2004, pp. 137–150. URL: http://www.usenix.org/events/osdi04/tech/dean.html
questions.qzh: 就两篇论文各写约 250 词讲解它的主题, 用恰当的引用和引语注明出处. a) 使用生成式 AI 生产力工具时的不耐烦和过度依赖 (CHI 2025); b) MapReduce (OSDI 2004).
questions.a:
写法要点: 第一次提到时点出作者并引用 (Dean and Ghemawat [1] introduced …); 转述用自己的话并给出处; 只把真正需要原话的地方 (定义、关键论断) 用引号直接引用, 引语要短, 标上页码; 区分「论文说的」和「你自己的评论」.

b) MapReduce 的可写内容: 用户只写两个函数, map 把输入的键值对变成中间键值对, reduce 把同一个键的所有中间值合并; 运行时系统负责切分输入、在集群上调度、处理机器故障和机器间通信, 所以没有并行和分布式经验的程序员也能用上大集群; 论文的例子包括统计词频和倒排索引. 摘要里对编程模型的那句定义很适合直接引用 (照原文抄并标 p. 137).

a) Qiao et al.: 先读摘要和结论, 弄清研究问题 (人们何时用、何时不用生成式 AI 工具, 以及不耐烦和过度依赖分别指什么)、研究方法 (实验还是访谈, 多少参与者) 和主要发现; 引语只引作者对这两个概念的定义. 不要替论文编数字, 所有数据都要能在原文里找到.

questions.q: Assessing Writing Advice. Read “The Young Person’s Guide to Writing Economic Theory,” available on Moodle, and describe its essence in an essay of about 300 words that answers the following questions: What are your main takeaways? Are there parts with which you disagree? What is specific to economic science and what also applies to computer science? William Thomson, Journal of Economic Literature 37(1), pp. 157–183, 1999.
questions.qzh: 读 Thomson 1999 年的《年轻人的经济理论写作指南》, 写约 300 词的短文: 主要收获是什么? 有没有不同意的地方? 哪些建议是经济学特有的, 哪些也适用于计 算机科学?
questions.a: 这是一篇读后感, 内容取决于你读到了什么, 这里只给组织方式: 第一段一句话概括文章 (面向谁、讲什么); 第二段挑两三条最有用的建议, 每条配一个你自己写作中的例子, 并和本课程讲过的内容对照 (例如记号、例子先于一般情形、标题和引言); 第三段写一条你不同意或认为过时的建议, 说明理由; 第四段区分学科: 经济理论的论文以定理和模型为主, 和理论计算机科学很接近, 记号和证明的建议基本通用; 而系统类、实证类的计算机论文还要考虑实验、代码和数据的呈现, 这是 Thomson 没有覆盖的. 引用文章里的观点时标出页码.

questions.q: Slide Competition. Among the material available on Moodle, you will find the slide decks for these presentations: Richard Yuanzhe Pang, Weizhe Yuan, Kyunghyun Cho, He He, Sainbayar Sukhbaatar, and Jason Weston, “Iterative Reasoning Preference Optimization,” NeurIPS 2024, 2024. ( https://neurips.cc/media/neurips-2024/Slides/96659_nZhhoGi.pdf ) Konstantin Fischer, Ivana Trummová, Phillip Gajland, Yasemin Acar, Sascha Fahl, and M. Angela Sasse, “The Challenges of Bringing Cryptography from Research Papers to Products,” USENIX Security 2024, 2024. ( https://www.usenix.org/system/files/usenixsecurity24_slides-fischer.pdf ) Patrizio Angelini, Therese Biedl, Markus Chimani, Sabine Cornelsen, Giordano Da Lozzo, Seok-Hee Hong, Giuseppe Liotta, Maurizio Patrignani, and Sergey Pupyrev, and Ignaz Rutter, and Alexander Wolff, “The Price of Upwardness,” GD 2024, 2024. ( https://ac.tuwien.ac.at/gd2024/slides/Session10-Patrizio-Angelini.pdf ) Have a look at the slides and briefly note what you consider their respective strengths and weaknesses. Discuss the slide decks and their respective strengths and weaknesses in groups of two or three, and rank the decks from strongest to weakest according to your collected arguments. Which arguments are the most important to you? Can you reach a consensus in your group?
questions.qzh: 看三份会议报告的幻灯片 (NeurIPS 的推理偏好优化、USENIX Security 的密码学从论文到产品、图绘制会议 GD 的「向上性的代价」), 记下各自的优缺点, 再分组讨论、 排名. 练习单上的标点错误 : 第 3 条的作者列表写成 「…, and Sergey Pupyrev, and Ignaz Rutter, and Alexander Wolff」, and 重复了三次. 正确写法是只在最后一位作者前用一次: 「…, Maurizio Patrignani, Sergey Pupyrev, Ignaz Rutter, and Alexander Wolff」.
questions.a: 评价没有标准答案, 关键是用第 12 讲的标准把理由说具体: 每页是否只有一个要点; 标题是不是完整的论断句 (assertion-evidence); 文字量 (能不能在讲者说话时读完); 图是否清晰、坐标轴是否标注; 有没有给出结构提示 (目录、进度); 字号和对比度在会场后排能否看清; 公式和术语是否为听众解释过; 结尾页是不是总结要点而不是「Thank you / Questions?」. 排名时说明你最看重哪一项, 例如「信息密度」和「视觉设计」冲突时你选哪个, 为什么.

questions.q: Poster Presentation. Among the material available on Moodle, you will find this scientific poster: Mayee F. Chen, Nicholas Roberts, Kush Bhatia, Jue Wang, Ce Zhang, Frederic Sala, and Christopher Ré, “Skill-it! A Data-Driven Skills Framework for Understanding and Training Language Models,” NeurIPS 2023, 2023. ( https://neurips.cc/media/PosterPDFs/NeurIPS 2023/72098.png ) Have a look at the poster and identify its domain and its main takeaway. Imagine that you are one of the poster’s authors, and develop a short script for a one-minute presentation of your poster to a professor who is an expert in the poster’s domain. Develop a slightly longer script for a two-minute presentation of the poster to a doctoral researcher who has just started working in the poster’s domain. Read both of your scripts to a neighbor, and have them read their scripts. Discuss your presentations, comparing them with respect to style and focus.
questions.qzh: 看一张 NeurIPS 2023 海报 (Skill-it!: 用「技能」的视角选择和排序训练数据来训练语言模型), 找出领域和核心结论; 假装你是作者, 分别为一位该领域的专家教授写一分钟讲稿、为一位刚入门的博士生写两分钟讲稿, 再和同桌互读、 比较.
questions.a:
两份讲稿的区别: 对专家, 开门见山讲贡献和与已有工作的差别, 背景一句带过, 直接指向海报上的关键结果图; 对新人, 先用一两句说明问题 (训练数据的顺序和配比会影响模型学到的能力), 解释关键术语 (这里的 skill 是什么意思、「技能之间有先后依赖」指什么), 再讲方法和结果, 最后说明这对他自己的研究可能有什么用.

两份都要: 第一句就说清「这张海报在说什么」; 边讲边指海报上对应的区域; 留出提问的空间. 讲稿里的数字和结论以海报为准, 不要凭印象补充.

questions.q: Slide Critique. Choose an old slide deck related to computer science that you have developed. If you do not have one or do not want to share one, find a slide deck on the internet. Write a 250-or-so-word critique of the slide deck that discusses its strengths and weaknesses. Sketch a poster based on the slide deck.
questions.qzh: 选一份自己做过的 (或网上找的) 计算机相关幻灯片, a) 写约 250 词的点评; b) 据此画一张海报草图.
questions.a: a) 点评可以沿用 12-1 的标准, 但要指名道姓: 「Slide 7 lists eleven bullet points」比「some slides are crowded」有用得多. b) 从幻灯片到海报不是把页面拼起来: 海报要能在讲者不在时被读懂, 所以要有一个一眼可见的核心结论 (大字标题或结论框); 按两到三栏从左到右、从上到下排; 每栏一个小标题; 幻灯片里的动画和逐步展开要换成一张完整的图; 文字比幻灯片多一些, 但每块不超过几行.

questions.q: Grasping grep. The grep tool is a command-line program that is available on Linux and similar systems. Make yourself familiar with the manual page, abbreviated as man page, for grep. You can access the man page by typing man grep in your terminal if you are working on a Linux-like system or by visiting https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/grep.1.html . Write a brief tutorial for grep of 200 to 400 words where you describe its purpose and explain its basic usage. In particular, explain how to search multiple files by using file-name patterns (such as grep hello *.txt ) and the -r option.
questions.qzh: 读 grep 的 man 页, 写一份 200 到 400 词的入门教程: 说明它的用途和基本用法, 特别要讲如何用文件名通配符 (如 grep hello *.txt ) 和 -r 选项搜索多个文件.
questions.a:
教程骨架 (英文正文, 每步一个可以直接复制运行的例子):

Finding Text with grep. grep prints every line of its input that matches a pattern. It is useful for finding where a function is used, which log entries contain an error, or which notes mention a topic.

Searching one file. grep error server.log prints all lines of server.log that contain error. Add -i to ignore case and -n to show line numbers: grep -in error server.log.

Searching several files. grep hello *.txt searches all files ending in .txt in the current directory. The shell, not grep, expands *.txt into a list of file names; grep then prefixes each match with the file name.

Searching a directory tree. grep -r hello notes/ searches every file in notes and its subdirectories. To restrict the search to certain files, combine it with --include: grep -r --include='*.txt' hello notes/. The quotes prevent the shell from expanding the pattern.

Patterns. The pattern is a regular expression: grep '^#' script.sh finds lines that start with #. Use -F to search for a fixed string that contains special characters, and -w to match whole words only.

要点 (第 13 讲): 教程以任务为导向, 先给最常用的情形; 每个命令都能运行; 解释容易踩坑的地方 (通配符是 shell 展开的, 所以 *.txt 不会进入子目录; 而 -r 不加 --include 会搜所有文件).

questions.q: Javadoc for a Number Queue Class. The WaitingList class is a Java implementation of a number queue system that can be used to manage people who are waiting for their turn. Write appropriate Javadoc comments for all public methods of the class and for the class itself. Make sure to include relevant @ tags. public class WaitingList { private List<Integer> items; private Random random; public WaitingList () { items = new ArrayList<>(); random = new Random(); } public void addNumber ( int number) { if (items. contains (number)) { throw new IllegalArgumentException( "Number " + number + " is already in the waiting list" ); } items. add (number); } public int addRandomNumber () { int number; do { number = random. nextInt ( 1000 ) + 1 ; } while (items. contains (number)); items. add (number); return number; } public Integer drawNumber () { if (items. isEmpty ()) { return null ; } return items. remove ( 0 ); } }
questions.qzh: WaitingList 是一个排队叫号系统: 可以加入指定号码、随机生成一个未用过的号码 (1 到 1000), 按先来先到的顺序叫号. 为这个类和所有 public 方法写 Javadoc, 用上合适的 @ 标签.
questions.a:
/**
 * A first-in, first-out queue of distinct ticket numbers for managing
 * people who wait for their turn.
 *
 * <p>Numbers are drawn in the order in which they were added. A number
 * can be in the list at most once. This class is not thread-safe.
 */
public class WaitingList {

    /** Creates an empty waiting list. */
    public WaitingList() { … }

    /**
     * Appends the given number to the end of the waiting list.
     *
     * @param number the number to add
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if {@code number} is already
     *         in the waiting list
     */
    public void addNumber(int number) { … }

    /**
     * Appends a randomly chosen number between 1 and 1000 (inclusive)
     * that is not yet in the waiting list, and returns it.
     *
     * <p>If all 1000 numbers are already in use, this method does not
     * terminate.
     *
     * @return the number that was added
     */
    public int addRandomNumber() { … }

    /**
     * Removes and returns the number at the front of the waiting list.
     *
     * @return the number that was added earliest, or {@code null} if the
     *         waiting list is empty
     */
    public Integer drawNumber() { … }
}

要点: 第一句是独立的摘要 (Javadoc 会把它放进方法总览); 写清楚边界情况: 号码范围是否包含 1000 (nextInt(1000) + 1 给出 1 到 1000)、空队列时返回 null 而不是抛异常; 写出读代码才能发现的陷阱: 1000 个号码都被占用时 addRandomNumber 会死循环. 文档如实写出这一点, 同时也该向维护者报告这个缺陷 (例如改为抛出 IllegalStateException). 构造器的注释可以很短, 但不能没有.

questions.q: Getting Started with Software. Choose some familiar piece of software (e.g., your favorite Python library). Write a brief getting-started guide of at most 300 words where you explain how to install the software. Include a description of how to create a “hello world” example and, if the word count allows for it, some slightly more complicated examples. Use pictures (e.g., screenshots, diagrams) where appropriate.
questions.qzh: 选一个熟悉的软件 (例如常用的 Python 库), 写一份不超过 300 词的入门指南: 怎么安装, 怎么写出「hello world」, 字数允许的话再给一两个稍复杂的例子, 适当配截图或示意图.
questions.a: 结构: ① 一句话说明这个软件做什么、这份指南面向谁、需要什么前提 (Python 版本、操作系统); ② 安装: 给出确切的命令 (例如 python3 -m pip install requests) 和验证安装是否成功的方法 (python3 -c "import requests; print(requests.__version__)"); ③ hello world: 最短的能运行的程序和它的预期输出; ④ 稍复杂的例子: 每个例子只引入一个新概念; ⑤ 下一步去哪里看 (官方教程、API 参考). 每段代码都要实际运行一遍再写进去, 输出照实贴出; 截图只在文字说不清时用 (例如 IDE 中的某个设置).
